newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end barely changed, still adrift.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end barely changed, still adrift.

text.p: The Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) ended barely changed on Thursday, with late foreign buying helping the index recover a 22 point dip, dealers said.
"There was a bit of UK interest this afternoon that helped prices to firm late in the day," one broker said.
The STII ended down 4.18 points at 2,043.71, rebounding from an intraday low of 2,025.15.
Market activity was sedate, with 133 million shares changing hands to see gainers and losers closely pegged at 166 to 173.
Dealers saw no major factors likely to give the market any firm direction during the week's remaining trading sessions.
Small capitalised stocks were again active, with fruit and vegetable supplier FHTK the most traded with 8.9 million shares changed to see it end up five cents at Singapore S$0.785.
Bank stocks OCBC and OUB were dented by the impact of bonus and rights issues respectively. OCBC ended down S$1.75 at S$8.05 and OUB closed down S$0.30 at S$5.30, both within market expectations.
Healthcare firm Parkway, thought by market sources to be a takeover target for DBS Land, ended down S$0.30 at S$6.60 on brisk volume of 1.3 million units.
